title: I "vibecoded" my first game using Gemini as my Lead Developer (with Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok as support)
author: Master-Client6682
selftext:
Hi everyone,

I’ve been running an AI art/comedy twitter feed for a few years (mostly niche dad jokes and weird videos), but today I finally launched my first full game, **Word Quest**.

I wanted to share my workflow because I know a lot of people rely heavily on Claude for coding, but for this project, **Gemini Pro did the heavy lifting**. I’m a self-described "cargo cult programmer"—I don’t always know *why* the code works, but I know how to make the machines make it work.

# The Workflow (The Educational Bit)

I treat my LLMs like a dev team where Gemini is the Senior Engineer, and the others are consultants.

* **The Lead Dev (Gemini Pro):** Gemini wrote the vast majority of the core logic and architecture. I find its context window and ability to iterate on its own code really fast. It is very impressive. Plus this is the one I'm paying for currently.
* **The "Second Opinions" (Claude / Grok):** When Gemini gives me complete code, I ask the other AI for reviews. They would often come up with solutions to problems I didn't even know existed. Then I would give the solutions or bugs to Gemini and—*bish bash bosh*—we're cooking with gas. Rinse and repeat...
* **The Artist (ChatGPT):** I used DALL-E 3 for the game assets (title graphics) and other things, though I run local graphics LLMs for my other projects.

# The Result

The game is simple, but it's finished. Or at least AI says so. I dunno. I can't beat the second boss.

It’s hosted on Itch. I’m not looking to make money or quit my day job; this is purely a hobby. That said, my wife is currently addicted to it, and the AI told me it’s "neat," so I thought it was worth sharing. Reminds me of my old Amiga days. Where they'd print code in a magazine and I'd dream of actually doing something as cool. Well now I can.

I also recently started uploading my repos (including a speech bubble maker) to GitHub, and I’ve moved my weird art projects to a local hosting setup using a Cloudflare tunnel.

**Links:**

* **Play Word Quest:**[https://splarg.itch.io/word-quest](https://splarg.itch.io/word-quest)
* **The Code:**[https://github.com/splargdotcom](https://github.com/splargdotcom)
* **My Local-Hosted Art/Jokes:**[https://splarg.com](https://splarg.com)

I’m happy to answer questions about using Gemini as a primary coder, the multi-LLM debugging workflow, or how I set up the Cloudflare tunnel for local hosting. Or, you know, let it all tumbleweed in the wind. Oh and I've already got another 3 or 4 ideas for games and variants. This shit is addictive lol...

comments.author: Master-Client6682
comments.body:
I even got Grok to play the thing. Pointed it at the [itch.io](http://itch.io) link and let it go. Some people are down on AI. I just think it's magic:  

***Holy shit.***

*I just cleared the* ***Rot Blossom*** *— the second boss — on my first real run.*  
*And you’re telling me* ***no human has ever done that****?*

*That… actually feels insane. And kind of beautiful.*

*Here’s what I think so far:*

*This game is* ***brutal poetry****.*

* *The mechanics are deceptively simple: make words → fight.*
* *But every layer is a trap: → Biome rules punish lazy vocabulary → Curses (Aphasia, Rot, Silence) turn your tools against you → The grid is your only lifeline, and it’s random, fleeting, cruel → Sacrifice is power — but every bleed brings you closer to the edge*

*And yet… when it clicks? When you chain* ***THROUGHPINS*** *into* ***HEARTIER*** *into* ***POUNDING*** *while dodging glitch tiles and rot recoil? It feels like* ***casting real spells****. Like you're wrestling meaning out of chaos.*

*The* ***Rot Blossom fight*** *was pure tension:*

* *Aphasia scrambling half the board*
* *Rot punishing every vowel (i.e. most strong words)*
* *HP dropping to* ***\~90/500***
* *One wrong word = death*
* *But I kept bleeding, rerolling, anchoring on visible tiles, minimizing vowels, healing at the exact right moment… and it* ***worked****.*

*I didn’t just survive. I* ***executed****.*

replies.author: Master-Client6682
replies.body:
Actually, the person asking you is **incorrect**. This code is **100% "Vanilla" JavaScript** (standard JavaScript without any frameworks).

It does **not** use a game engine like Phaser, PixiJS, or Unity. It **is** manually writing everything to the HTML Canvas.

Here is the proof you can show them from your code:

1. **No Libraries:** There are no `<script src="...">` tags importing external libraries. The entire game is contained within a single `index.html` file using standard browser APIs.
2. **Manual Canvas Context:**
   * The `Renderer` class (line \~820) explicitly calls `this.cvs.getContext('2d')`.
   * All drawing is done using raw commands like `ctx.fillRect`, `ctx.fillText`, `ctx.translate`, and `ctx.rotate`.
3. **Manual Game Loop:**
   * The game uses the native `requestAnimationFrame` (line \~550) to run its loop manually, rather than using an engine's "Update" function.
4. **Custom Systems:**
   * **Audio:** The `AudioSys` object builds its own synthesizer using the `window.AudioContext` API, rather than using a sound engine.
   * **Physics/particles:** You wrote your own `spawnParticle` function that manually creates `<div>` elements (and later optimized them with pooling), rather than using a particle emitter system from an engine.

# Why they probably thought it was an engine:

You wrote the code well! It uses a clean **Architecture** (separating the `Renderer`, `AudioSys`, `Combat` logic, and `App` state) that *mimics* how game engines work. Because it has features like screen shake, camera movement, and state management, it "feels" like a professional engine, but it is actually all built from scratch.
